classification.difficultyReason: The student reads fractions off two bar models (2/4 and 2/6), fills a guided same/different statement, then decides which bar shows more of its whole. This needs a link between equal shaded lengths and unequal wholes, plus a comparison of 1/2 with 1/3. Part b scaffolds the key idea, so it is less demanding than an open explanation like p20-q10. It is above routine reading of diagrams.

content.prompt: Kai has drawn two bar models.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Write the fraction of each bar that is shaded.

answer.worked:
The upper bar has $4$ equal parts with $2$ shaded, so $\frac{2}{4}$.

The lower bar has $6$ equal parts with $2$ shaded, so $\frac{2}{6}$.

inlines.text: length, but the whole bars are

answer.worked: Both shaded parts are $3$ cm long. The whole bars are $6$ cm and $9$ cm long.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Which bar shows more of its whole?

answer.worked:
The upper bar shows $3$ cm out of $6$ cm, which is half of its whole.

The lower bar shows $3$ cm out of $9$ cm, which is one third of its whole.

The same shaded length is a bigger part of a shorter whole, so the upper bar shows more of its whole.
